reading_comprehension_tests.excerpt: Council we held and took running meat aboard for our lives, but the captain, he says, “We are short of hands, and we must make the best of what we have.” To pull a rope or to stand a watch was past my power, but I could carry bread and cheese, and help the doctor with his bandages. metadata.author: H. G. Wells
metadata.focus_standard: Chronological setting mechanics, visual concealment theory, & physiological distress tracing

reading_comprehension_tests.excerpt: The stranger came early in February, out of a biting wind and a driving snow, the last snowfall of the year, over the down, walking from Bramblehurst railway station, and carrying a little black portmanteau in his thickly gloved hand. He was wrapped up from head to foot, and the brim of his soft felt hat hid every inch of his face but the shiny tip of his nose; the snow had piled itself against his shoulders and chest, and added a white crest to the burden he carried. He staggered into the 'Coach and Horses' more dead than alive, and flung his portmanteau down.

options.D: He travels late at night in autumn to avoid encountering local law enforcement

questions.explanation: Arriving 'early in February' amidst 'a biting wind and a driving snow' on foot from a railway station establishes immediate theme points of severe isolation and vulnerability to nature.

options.B: Physical snow accumulating on top of the bag he is holding

questions.explanation: The text links environment to his property, tracking how 'snow had piled itself against his shoulders and chest, and added a white crest to the burden [the portmanteau/bag] he carried.'
